narrative.overview:
TripLens tells City decisions the way they would be read aloud at a 1970s Toronto kitchen table. Each scene owns the whole screen in one flat colour from the kitchen (harvest gold, avocado, burnt orange, walnut, Pyrex turquoise), and the ink flips between dark coffee brown and cream so the words always sit on the field at body-text contrast. Nothing floats on a card; the page is a stack of full-width colour courses, and the background colour itself changes as the reader scrolls (0.9s cross-fade), so the scene change is the section break.

The world's one picture is a round stoneware platter of the neighbourhood: a walnut centre with wood rings, an avocado glaze edge, a dotted stoneware band, a turquoise dashed bus route, and flat, rounded houses, trees, stops and a cream bus standing on its rim. It turns like a lazy Susan, one scene per scroll. Drawings are flat fills with rounded corners and short dark-brown strokes, never outlines with gradients, never photographs.

Density is low and type is large: the body never drops below 20px, the display face is a warm, soft-shouldered serif, and every control is a chunky pill at 56px or taller. The register is warm and plain, never alarming.
keyCharacteristics: One colour field per scene; the field is the background of the whole viewport, nav included.
Ink is either coffee brown or cream (teal ink on turquoise), chosen per field for contrast.
Pills that invert: the primary action is always ink-on-field reversed (field-coloured text on an ink pill).
Flat stoneware drawing language; the platter is the only illustration.
Large, legible type: Young Serif display, Atkinson Hyperlegible body at 20px and up.
Figures are read on one measured scale against the rider's limit.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: A scene owns the whole screen in one field colour. Never place two fields side by side on one screen, and never set a field colour as a small accent on another field.

rules.name: The Ink Flip Rule
rules.body: Every field has exactly one ink, and everything on it (text, rules, pills, scale bar, focus ring, selection) uses that ink or that field. Ink is chosen for at least 4.5:1 at body size; secondary text uses full ink, not a faded one, on avocado, orange and turquoise.

rules.name: The Drawing Palette Rule
rules.body: The platter drawing uses the same hues, lifted slightly brighter so it reads against its own field (gold #f0c04a, orange #e07a3a, avocado #8a9b3a, turquoise #4fb0a8, walnut #5a3a22, wood #6b4428 / #7a5032, leaf shade #6f7f2c). These are drawing-only; never use them for text or page fields.

rules.name: The Twenty Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Running text, notes, sources and labels are 20px or larger. Smaller sizes appear only on aria-hidden decoration (scale tick numbers, 16px).

rules.name: The Sentence Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines are full plain sentences with a full stop, in sentence case. No small labels or eyebrows above them.

rules.name: The Flat Stoneware Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat colour. Lift is expressed by motion (a pill rises 3px on hover), never by a shadow.

dos: **Do** give each scene one full-screen field from the palette and flip the ink to the shipped pair for that field.
**Do** make the primary action a 64px ink pill with field-coloured text and an arrow, one per screen.
**Do** keep running text at 20px or larger in Atkinson Hyperlegible, and headlines as plain sentences in Young Serif.
**Do** show any distance against the rider's limit on the scale bar, with a plain-sentence verdict beside it.
**Do** draw in flat, rounded stoneware shapes using the drawing palette, with a text description.
**Do** honour reduced motion: colour changes and the platter snap rather than ease.
donts: **Don't** use white, grey, or a white civic page with a headline, button and three feature cards.
**Don't** add drop shadows, gradients, glass or blur to page elements.
**Don't** put small labels or eyebrows above headlines.
**Don't** use faded or translucent ink for text on avocado, orange or turquoise fields.
**Don't** bring outline-style icon sets or glyph icons into this world; the platter drawing and the inline SVG arrow are the vocabulary.
